analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES TSMC Terafab talks; DSY read from Schneider; BT acquires TalkTalk; DT AI CMD; AI Credit; Q3 semis preview
key_insights: TSMC hit an all-time high after Elon Musk confirmed preliminary talks on a TSMC role in Terafab's Texas chip project (initial investment US$16.8bn, total spending US$55-119bn). A partnership could reduce execution risk but complicate Intel's role. No agreement has been reached.
TSMC's 15 October call is the next catalyst for updates on capex, CoWoS, Texas and pricing. ASML reports the day before.

GIR's Q3 US semis preview is constructive after the SOX's 11% pullback over two months. Expectations are more achievable and upside is likely across most sub-sectors. Preferred: SemiCap, compute, select analog and memory/storage. AMAT, STX and MCHP are preferred into earnings. QCOM, KLAC and WDC are less attractive on a relative basis.

Schneider Electric agreed to acquire PTC at $205/share, all cash. Equity value is ~$22.6B and EV ~$23.7B, a ~42% premium to last close. GS says this raises the bar for Dassault Systemes (DSY) without being existential. DSY keeps differentiation in multi-physics simulation and complex long-cycle verticals.

DSY is a consensus short, so M&A validation of the sector carries squeeze risk near term. Medium term, DSY faces pressure to accelerate its data/AI layer or lose share in contested deals. A takeover of DSY is not simple because the Dassault family controls ~39.9-40.5%.

BT confirmed the acquisition of TalkTalk and PlatformX out of administration on a debt-free basis. Estimated FY27 cash impact is c£400m, including a c£60m trading loss and non-receipt of c£100m owed to Openreach. BT reiterated underlying FY27 and multi-year guidance. Regulatory review and execution risk remain.

DT's AI Investor Event in Bonn targets ~€800m of AI-related revenue from non-US enterprise customers by 2030 and ~€2.5bn of indirect cost savings versus 2023. Guidance and medium-term targets were confirmed.

Ben Snider: consensus expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y, with AI beneficiaries accounting for more than half of it and hyperscaler capex up 116%. Median stock EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth is expected to accelerate to 55% in Q3.

US L/S net leverage fell for a third consecutive week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and approaching the 2nd percentile of 5-year lows. Europe saw its largest percentage net buying in over five years.

AI credit (Adam Crook): hyperscaler debt issuance is estimated at ~$250bn in 2026 (under $20bn in 2024) and $420bn in 2027. Hyperscalers are only ~40% of the >$575bn of global AI-related debt issuance this year. Issuance is shifting to shorter maturities. GS rates strategists say the supply reduces appetite for duration and raises the risk that long-term yields overshoot fair value.

Europe media: holdco media growth has returned to ~6% in 2Q26 from ~3% in 2025, with little in-housing. Key risk is digital-native independent agencies winning accounts below $200m of media budget. Publicis is least exposed, WPP and Omnicom more. GIR upgraded Stagwell to Buy ($13 target, 54% upside) and initiated Havas at Neutral (€19 target, 8% upside).

SIA data: August IC shipments ex-memory rose ~2% m/m, ahead of seasonal norms. Total semiconductor shipments run ~10% above long-term trend on a three-month average, up from 7% in July. Analog shipments are also ~10% above trend. GS is most positive on Microchip, NXP and Analog Devices.

Memory: NVDA may secure only ~60% of its 2027 LPDDR5X needs, which could halve Vera Rubin SOCAMM capacity. A full NVL72 rack needs ~54TB. Tight supply could sustain PC and smartphone price pressure through 1H27, with memory potentially near 40% of smartphone BOM.

The US may phase in restrictions on Chinese optical modules starting at 3.2T, possibly as early as October. Imports could stay permitted if at least 65% of BOM value is from US companies. Current 800G and 1.6T products reportedly fall outside the initial scope.
Quanta reportedly suspended HP notebook production for a week in September to negotiate higher prices. Servers were over 80% of Quanta's 2Q26 revenue.

Marvell sees 3-4+ custom-chip opportunities per XPU. Inference-driven KV-cache demand is up ~10x in nine months. Some sell side sees ASIC/XPU shipment share at 54% in 2027 and 55% in 2028. AVGO and Marvell hold ~90% of the custom AI ASIC market.
UK CMA found the nexfibre/Netomnia deal could substantially reduce competition in wholesale broadband. GS views this as incrementally negative for VMO2 (TEF/LBTYA) and BT.
AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are forming a joint venture to pool spectrum and standards for direct-to-device satellite coverage, a response to Starlink. No service date or venture name yet.
Auto1's 3Q pre-close missed: units sold ~4% below consensus and adjusted EBITDA ~10% below. GS cut 2026/27 EBITDA forecasts by c.4%/6%, kept Buy, and cut the price target to €32 from €37.
Outdoor advertising: JCDecaux is best positioned. GS is slightly ahead of consensus on 3Q26 organic growth with more upside in Q4. Stroeer is in line on revenue and EBITDA.

US trading: NDX hit a new ATH while rates capped risk appetite. S&P is down seven straight weeks per the desk, with concentration in Tech. Semis saw demand after solid MU earnings and NVDA's larger buyback plans. Little willingness to chase despite light positioning.

GS Prime: fundamental L/S managers -0.3% on the week, -0.6% in September, +12.7% YTD. Systematic L/S +1.0% on the week, +3.5% in September, +20.8% YTD. Europe was the most net bought region for a third week. Comm Services, Consumer Discretionary and Info Tech were the most net sold sectors.
Fiserv Small Business Index: September spending growth rose 2.2% SA versus 1.2% in August. Transactions fell 2.0% y/y while average ticket rose 4.3% y/y.

OpenAI safety employee David Robinson resigned, citing a culture that prioritises rapid iterative deployment over rigorous safeguards. OpenAI says it is strengthening security, third-party testing and monitoring.

Auto1: target cut to €32 from €37 after weak 3Q pre-close and c.4%/6% EBITDA cuts for 2026/27. Buy kept on Autohero re-acceleration and market-share gains.

tension_points.bull_case: M&A validation of industrial software lifts the space and DSY is a consensus short, so a squeeze is possible. DSY keeps differentiation in multi-physics simulation and long-cycle verticals.
tension_points.bear_case: A scaled Schneider + PTC + AVEVA + Cognite stack raises competitive intensity. DSY must accelerate its data/AI layer or lose share, and a takeover is hard with ~40% family control.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 S&P EPS growth of 27% consensus, hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerating to 55%, and most companies expected to beat.
tension_points.bear_case: AI debt supply (~$250bn hyperscaler issuance in 2026) could push long-end yields higher, and confidence depends on improving returns on invested capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings failing to show improving returns on invested capital through stronger revenue growth and cloud profitability.
